sam (devex): FYI hitting a nasty combo of pnpm workspace + exports map + edge dev server. Sample app crashes when importing SDK in the edge worker: 

sam (devex): Runtime error: Uncaught ReferenceError: exports is not defined
importing with `const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk')` in a legacy example, but we expect ESM import to be used in edge.

lee (eng-runtime): that error usually means a CJS file got evaluated as ESM or vice versa. Can you share the SDK package.json exports and how the sample app resolves the package (symlinked workspace vs installed)? Node/pnpm versions?

sam (devex): pnpm 8.5, node 18.17, edge dev server uses esbuild-based bundler with rollup plugin. Monorepo workspace, `@redwood/sdk` is a workspace package (symlinked). SDK package.json excerpt: ```json
{"name":"@redwood/sdk","version":"0.11.0","main":"dist/cjs/index.cjs","module":"dist/esm/index.mjs","types":"dist/index.d.ts","exports":{"./package.json":"./package.json","./dist/esm/index.mjs":"./dist/esm/index.mjs"}}```

sam (devex): sample-app uses `const { createClient } = require('@redwood/sdk')` in old examples; newer examples use `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'`. Both blow up in the edge dev server at build time or runtime depending on path.

mira (eng-ml): two likely issues: 1) exports doesn't expose the package root (".") so tooling that resolves the package root can't find the default entry; 2) bundlers that follow exports strictly may fall back to loading packaged cjs/esm files directly and produce mixed module systems.

aldo (devex): for edge we want native ESM. That means package.json should have an explicit "." export with an import condition pointing at the .mjs entry. For compatibility with require-ing code in Node CJS consumers, add a require mapping to the cjs build. Something like: ```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}```

sam (devex): ok that maps to previous advice. Two follow-ups: 1) why does the bundler still complain about "exports not found for './package.json'" when I add the mapping? 2) Types still not picked up by TS in the workspace consumer.

lee (eng-runtime): bundlers sometimes attempt to read package.json via the package subpath to discover exports or version fields. If your exports map doesn't include './package.json' explicitly, some bundlers will error. You already included it so the error points to a cached node_modules resolution from other workspace packages. Try clearing pnpm store or running a full reinstall. Also check whether the bundler resolves the symlink target path (preserve-symlinks) and if the target package.json has the exports map.

mira (eng-ml): TS issue: editors/tsserver will look at the `types` field at package root or the `exports['.'].types` conditional. Some tools don't support conditional `types` fields yet. Best practice: keep a top-level `types` pointing to the d.ts (e.g., "types":"dist/index.d.ts") and ensure that file exists when using the workspace (i.e., build step before launching editor).

aldo (devex): also consider shipping a tiny `index.js` at the package root that re-exports the proper ESM entry for dev environments (only in source repo, not published). Example: `export * from './dist/esm/index.mjs'` when using native ESM, or `module.exports = require('./dist/cjs/index.cjs')` for legacy. But that adds maintenance overhead. Prefer leaning on clean exports mapping + CI check that workspace works.

sam (devex): weird gotcha: rollup plugin for the edge server insists on resolving package.json and fails if exports contains only explicit subpath entries. After adding the root mapping it moved forward but the edge worker still failed with `ReferenceError: exports is not defined` at runtime when the worker imported the cjs bundle. I think rollup included the CJS file into the ESM bundle due to the require mapping.

lee (eng-runtime): yep that indicates the bundler pulled the CJS entry. For edge, prefer import-only flows. If you set `exports['.'].import` to the .mjs entry and ensure your app uses `import`, the bundler will choose ESM. Remove the require mapping only if you don't need CJS consumers. Alternatively, instruct the bundler to prefer ESM (esbuild/rollup commonjs plugin config).

sam (devex): short-term workaround: updated SDK package.json to expose root export with import -> dist/esm/index.mjs, removed require mapping, added `types: "dist/index.d.ts"`, rebuilt and restarted edge dev server. Sample app works with `import` but legacy `require` examples break.

mira (eng-ml): for our deprecation plan, let's standardize docs: examples in the sample-app should use ESM import for edge samples and add a note that CJS require is deprecated for edge targets. Create a migration note and a checklist item for SDK releases to validate ESM entry semantics across workspaces and edge bundlers.

aldo (devex): I'll open a small PR to sample-app updating docs, and add a CI job that: 1) builds SDK, 2) installs sample-app as workspace consumer (symlink), 3) runs edge dev bundler to ensure no CJS leakage.

ci-bot: queued pipeline job: workspace-edge-exports-smoke-test (expected ~3m)

sam (devex): thanks. I'll also add a short devex doc on pnpm workspace quirks: mention `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile` when switching node versions, clear `node_modules/.pnpm` caches if exports change, and guidance on preserve-symlinks when debugging.

lee (eng-runtime): one more: add a tiny test in the SDK repo that loads the published package with a simple bundler (esbuild) in both symlink and installed modes. Catches these mistakes early.

sam (devex): will do. Filing the PR + issue with reproduction steps and logs. Thanks :v:
